subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: FinPay discovery — latency & throughput needs

Hi Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps.

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Latency: target p95 < 120 ms for inference (goal: p95 < 100 ms where possible), 99th < 200 ms on peak
- Throughput: baseline ~800 req/s, expected steady growth to 1.5k req/s within 3 months; short bursts to ~2k req/s
- Data residency: US-only; standard SOC2 controls required
- Model profile: mixed short prompts + streaming responses for fraud alerts (avg seq len ~120 tokens)

Options and trade-offs (high level):
- Hosted API: Fastest time-to-value, managed autoscaling and streaming. Good if you want to start quickly and operate on usage pricing. Latency is generally good for moderate throughput, but p95 during sustained peaks can vary unless you reserve capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Predictable throughput and latency SLOs, lower per-token unit costs at scale, and isolation of capacity. Recommended for sustained 1k+ req/s workloads where consistent p95 is important.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Only needed if FinPay has strict network or compliance constraints beyond SOC2 (e.g., PCI isolation or on-prem requirement).

Recommendation: Given the throughput growth and strict p95 target, I recommend we scope a 2-week Dedicated PoC (reserved pool sizing + load test) to validate p95 and cost. If you'd prefer a faster ramp, we can start on Hosted with a targeted reserved throughput window while we prepare Dedicated sizing.

Next steps:
1) Marissa (solutions) to propose initial Dedicated sizing and expected p95 targets — I’ve attached a sizing doc.
2) Pricing/commit options: I’ll attach a pricing sheet for Hosted vs Dedicated and examples of commit levels.
3) Schedule a short sizing + engineering sync (30–45m) — propose Tue 11/4 or Wed 11/5.

Let me know which path you prefer and availability for the sizing call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock in the sizing call: 

- For the Dedicated PoC, what kind of baseline node/pool sizing maps to ~1.5k steady req/s with p95 < 120 ms? Any ballpark so we can align internal infra stakeholders?
- If we start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated, how seamless is the migration? Do we expect model/version pinning or client-side changes?
- Pricing: can you share a comparison for 3-month commit vs pay-as-you-go hosted for the volumes above? We’re evaluating cost and time-to-value.

Also, can you confirm that streaming responses and KV cache behavior are the same between Hosted and Dedicated (we rely on prefix caching a lot)?

Appreciate the fast turnaround — we want to present clear options to our engineering and procurement teams next week.

— Alex
Alex Carter
Director of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.carter@finpay.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinPay discovery — latency & throughput needs

Alex — great questions, see answers below. Looping Marissa for sizing details and Dylan for pricing/contract path.

1) Baseline sizing (ballpark):
- A starting Dedicated pool equivalent to ~8x A100-class capacity (we call it "dedicated S2" in internal sizing) typically supports ~1.2–1.8k req/s for short/medium sequences with p95 in the 70–120 ms range depending on model and batching. For your mix (avg length ~120 tokens + streaming), we’d target 8–12 GPU-equivalent nodes for safety during the PoC. Marissa — can you confirm with the specific model we benchmarked and update the sizing doc?

2) Migration path (Hosted -> Dedicated):
- Seamless from an API standpoint. Same API surface and model versioning; you can pin model versions. Migration is largely a config and routing change on our side — no client code changes required unless you want to flip to a private endpoint. We also provide a canary rollout approach so traffic can be shifted gradually.

3) Streaming & KV cache parity:
- Streaming behavior and KV/prefix caching are supported on both Hosted and Dedicated. Differences are operational: on Dedicated you control autoscaling policies and cache residency which can improve p95 consistency.

4) Pricing (high level):
- Hosted PAYG: simple per-token + egress; better short-term TTV but higher unit cost at sustained scale.
- Dedicated (3-month commit examples): significantly lower per-token cost (15–30% lower depending on commit) and predictable monthly capacity fees. I attached a pricing sheet with a 3-month and 12-month illustrative comparison. Dylan — can you push the tailored pricing for FP-2026-042 after we confirm sizing?

Suggested next step: Marissa to confirm exact Dedicated node count for the model and provide an expected p95 projection; Dylan to deliver a pricing comparison for 3-month commit vs hosted. Once we have both, Alex we can schedule the 30–45m sizing + procurement sync.

Thanks — Neha
